policy.hypothesis: Using same-precatalyst transfer, Morpholine-AlPhos will favor high-temperature candidates with moderate base equivalents (~1.1-1.5 or ~2.0) and medium-to-long residence times; therefore at least one of the selected high-temperature candidates should outperform the lower-temperature same-precatalyst quality anchor.

policy.revised_hypothesis: For Morpholine-AlPhos, moderate base equivalents (~1.1-1.5) and high temperature (~100 C) with long residence times yield moderate product formation, but the maximum achievable yield is lower than in Aniline-AlPhos or Benzamide-AlPhos campaigns. Lower temperature and shorter residence time conditions are suboptimal. The optimal base identity may differ from BTMG, and exploring alternative bases such as BTTP or MTBD could improve yields. Therefore, further exploration of base identity and residence time at high temperature is necessary to identify improved conditions.

failure_conditions: If Morpholine-AlPhos fundamentally prefers a different base identity regime than prior AlPhos substrates, especially BTTP or MTBD over BTMG, this design can miss the optimum.
If morpholine reactivity is much more temperature-sensitive than aniline/benzamide under AlPhos, the 47.5 C probe may underperform and weaken transfer.
If the target optimum requires very short residence time at 100 C rather than medium/long times, candidates 018 and 009 may be too slow.
If same-precatalyst transfer is less informative than broader cross-substrate amine trends, selecting only BTMG candidates may limit early learning.
If the elevated catalyst loading in the target changes the ranking of numeric conditions relative to prior AlPhos campaigns, transferred preferences may not hold.
